data: Starship (Super Heavy + Starship upper stage, expended)

© SpaceX — Mars architecture target for the late-2026 window. Dropped: on 2026-02-08 Elon Musk said SpaceX would focus on the Moon and start on Mars in about five to seven years (CNN, ABC News). Dates are the original late-2026 target.
Musk clips his Mars settlement ambition, aims for the moon instead — CNN (2026-02-09)
First fully reusable launch system to attempt Mars landing

An uncrewed demonstration of the Starship Mars architecture: launch on Super Heavy, refill in LEO from a tanker variant, then trans-Mars injection of a fully-fuelled Starship and powered descent to the Martian surface. SpaceX aimed for the late-2026 Mars window. In February 2026 Elon Musk put the Moon first and said work on Mars would start in about five to seven years, dropping the late-2026 target; no new date has been set. A Mars Starship would land about a hundred tonnes at a time, against a few thousand kilograms for today's landers.
Starship from Boca Chica or Cape Canaveral — first super-heavy interplanetary launch.
Tanker rendezvous and propellant transfer in LEO over multiple flights.
Trans-Mars injection from fully-fuelled LEO state.
Powered descent to Mars surface — no parachutes, no airbags, no sky-crane.
